title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally
author: Zhizhuo Kou, Jian Yang, Pengfei Hao, Junyu Luo et al.
description: When a speaker says ``some students passed'', listeners infer that not all of them did. Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences. We study this directly: we keep a model's weights fixed, change only how much…
summary: When a speaker says ``some students passed'', listeners infer that not all of them did. Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences.
takeaways: Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences.
A second tool cuts the model's own reasoning at successive points and asks for an answer, showing where the reading changes.

Thinking makes models read logical words as logic: it cancels the implicatures of some (not all) and or (not both) in most tested open reasoning models and in GPT-5, while context-driven inferences such as indirect answers improve.
